title.narrative: Boosting agricultural productivity to reduce hunger among rural poor in Moyamba district of Sierra Leone

description.narrative: Impact: 30 communities in the chiefdoms of Kargboro, Ribbi and Upper Banta in Moyamba have improved their food, nutrition and hygiene security. Objective: 2,010 smallholder farmer household (51% of 12,060 overall household members are women) in the chiefdoms of Kargboro, Ribbi and Upper Banta in the Moyamba district are using the skills they have acquired to improve their livelihoods.

Problem statement: High food and nutrition insecurity in Sierra Leone: Serious gender inequality, lack of inputs and coordinated actions leading to poverty, hunger and inequality.Target group and districts: 2000 poor rural households (12,2000 persons, incl. women, youth and other marginalised groups) in Moyamba District.Project Objective: Improved socio-economic wellbeing of rural smallholder farmers and marginalised groups affected by grabbing by foreign private companies. Outputs: Improved agricultural productivity; Climate smart agricultural practices adopted; Local seeds and market systems developed; Advocacy for responsible land use and right to food; Partner Capacity Development for advocacy and social accountability developedPartners: SiLNoRF and WellFound (new partner)

The project targets the most vulnerable people in Moyamba District: women, children, people with disabilities and the unemployed, with a strong focus on social integration and community-wide development. The project is being implemented in 30 villages in three chiefdoms in Moyamba District: Kargboro, Ribbi and Upper Banta. The total population in these three chiefdoms is 64,532, of which a total of 2,010 families/households (=12,060 household members benefitting in total, based on an average household size of 6) have been selected as the direct target group. 51% of overall household members are women and 49% are men (as per City Population, 2021). 2010 individuals are selected in the project as representatives of the target households, they are not necessarily heads of households, but chosen based on discussions at household level to see who is most suitable to coordinate participation of themselves and other household members for project activities. This way, the project team can also ensure that women have a higher proportion of representation. In some households, the heads of households are very old, so they can select a representative for their household.
